reasons: F23, F21: Went public via SPAC or reverse merger within 3 years and is raising capital, so there is pressure to show growth to investors, and young post-SPAC issuers have a higher base rate of misstatement.

R04, R02, R15: Sales grew about 3.3x while the gross margin index swung sharply (-182, meaning gross margin flipped sign) and ROA fell 0.41. That fits an early-stage, loss-making scale-up, where valuations depend heavily on judgement.
R08, R17: Total accruals are high at 20% of assets, and the Dechow F-score (1.09) is just above the 1.0 threshold. Both point to somewhat elevated misstatement risk.
R07, R13: Leverage rose sharply (LVGI 3.67) and the soft-assets share is very high (1.0), so the balance sheet is exposed to impairment and valuation judgements.
F27, F24: A significant inventory writedown and a CAM classed as 'other' point to valuation areas (inventory, possibly long-lived assets) where estimates may be wrong.

R19, F01, F05, F07, F16, F17, F19: Mitigating factors. Operating cash flow tracks net income (CFO/NI 1.07), there is no material weakness, no auditor change, no prior-period correction, no SEC inquiry, no class action and no covenant issues. F03 shows no ICFR auditor attestation (likely an emerging growth company), so internal controls get less outside checking.
